free_tier.stated: HotDebrid premium link generator is free and unlimited (feature list); the FAQ states 'each single user is able to leech up to 8 premium links per day'. HotDebrid premium leech is compatible with over +100 cloud file hosts.
free_tier.notes: The feature list says 'free and unlimited'; the FAQ gives a per-user limit of 8 premium links per day ('At the moment'), so 'unlimited' describes bandwidth and file size, not the number of links. No host list, status page or terms page is published.

per_object_cap.stated: There is no absurd file size limits. (vendor)

retention.stated: We will remove your file links after the premium download has finished.

egress.terms: We don't limit your download bandwidth in any way. (vendor) No allowance, no counter and no measured throughput is published.

interface_detail: One web form: paste a link, click Generate Premium Link, receive a download link. No API, no plugin, no documented endpoint.
tooling: Browser only; no extension, plugin, API or CLI is published.
chaining: A published ceiling of 8 premium links per day per user can be planned against, but no host list is published, so a client cannot know whether a needed host is covered.

limits.value: the generated premium link is 'locked to a single user IP'; no numeric limit published
up to 8 premium links per day per user ('At the moment')

limits_note: Two sibling sites, okdebrid.com and anydebrid.com, publish the same feature list, the same FAQ shape and the same 'free and unlimited' claim with different sentences, so they are not copies. None of the three publishes a host list or a status page; only HotDebrid's FAQ was re-read and it gives a per-user quota of 8 premium links per day.
binding_note: The FAQ states up to 8 premium links per day per user, the only numeric limit published; file size and bandwidth are stated as unlimited, and no throughput was measured.

identity_cost.detail: No account and no email is requested on the page; the generator takes a link only.

reliability_note: Ad-funded with no status page and no published host list, so a dead host and a banned client look the same from outside; links are IP-locked.
confidence_note: The vendor's own page is captured and quoted for each field. The 8 links per day figure is a stated limit; 'unlimited' elsewhere on the page is a claim, and no unlock or throughput was measured. No host list is published.

evidence.proved: 'free and unlimited', 'compatible with over +100 cloud file hosts', 'We don't limit your download bandwidth in any way', 'The provided premium link is locked to a single user IP', and the absence of any host list or numeric limit on the page
the FAQ states a per-user limit of 8 premium links per day
evidence.quote: At the moment, each single user is able to leech up to 8 premium links per day.

evidence.proved: the page states no per-file size cap
evidence.quote: Our premium downloader is not capped by file size limitations.

evidence.proved: links are removed after the leech ends
evidence.quote: Your premium links are automatically removed once you end leeching the file.

evidence.proved: the vendor states no bandwidth limit
evidence.quote: Max download speed, 100% guaranteed! We don't limit your download bandwidth in any way.

evidence.proved: the first step of the flow takes a link and no account
evidence.quote: Input your link in the field above.

evidence.proved: the generated link is locked to one user IP
evidence.quote: The provided premium link is locked to a single user IP, only you may have access to it.

notes: They are not counted as separate capacity. This class is why answer cannot be 'free is unlimited': the claim is free to make and unverifiable from outside.
